tickets.title: Add yourself to the team directory
tickets.summary: The People page has an empty spot reserved for you. Fill it in, on a branch, with a commit message I can respect.
steps: In your real terminal, inside the `the-studio` folder, start from fresh main: `git switch main` then `git pull`
Create your branch: `git switch -c onboarding/add-<your-name>` (lowercase, dashes, no spaces)
Open `src/content/team.ts` and replace `null` in `newHire` with your entry. Save, then check the People page in the app.
Look before you leap: `git status` and `git diff`
Stage and commit: `git add src/content/team.ts` then `git commit -m "..."` with a message that would survive Commit Court
Publish your branch: `git push -u origin onboarding/add-<your-name>`
Tell your coach **done** in the project thread. Stuck? Say **hint**.
acceptance: It has a commit that changes only `src/content/team.ts`
The commit message passes Commit Court: imperative, capitalized, no period, 50 characters or fewer
`favoriteToken` is a real token name (Dot will check, and so will TypeScript)
`main` is untouched. Nobody pushes to main.

Hi! I'm Dot. I keep the design system honest. We use **shadcn/ui**, and all of our tokens live in one file: `src/styles/tokens.css`. Components only ever reference those. If you're ever unsure whether something is a token, run `npm run dot` and I'll tell you. (It's a script. It's also me.)

Gus. Senior engineer. I review commits. Most of them disappoint me.
Do the Day 1 lesson in Studio Academy first. Then you get a ticket.
You passed the lesson. Fine. Here's your first ticket. Small, real, and I will be reading your commit message very carefully.

choices.text: What makes a commit message LGTM-worthy to you?

replies.text: Specific. Imperative. Short. Tells me **what** changed, and in the body, **why**, if it isn't obvious. Like a good layer name.

choices.text: Can I just push straight to main? It's a tiny change.

replies.text: No. Nobody pushes to main. Bjorn pushes to main. Do you want to be Bjorn?
